blocks.html: Dispersion (variability, spread) is the second half of descriptive statistics: how scattered the values are around their centre. Two datasets can share a mean and still describe very different realities (§3.1). This chapter builds the measures of spread in rising order of refinement: the range (§3.2), quartiles, percentiles and the interquartile range (§3.3–3.4), the mean deviation (§3.5), variance and standard deviation (§3.6–3.7), and the coefficient of variation (§3.8). It ends with two measures of shape, skewness (§3.9) and kurtosis (§3.10).
